Markdown nests no deeper than markdown-it's maxNesting, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.gwww)

Deep nesting overflowed the stack: `>` and list markers recursed per
level, link labels nested per `[`, and inline rendering recursed per
emphasis level. Each now follows Rich:

- Blocks stop at markdown-it's maxNesting (20; a quote one level, a list
  and its item one each). Past it a container's content is an `unread`
  token that draws nothing, and a list item that deep takes every line to
  the end of its quote or document, as markdown-it's does.
- Link labels are scanned as markdown-it's parseLinkLabel/skipToken scans
  them, with its per-position cache and its level cap. A link whose label
  holds a link is refused (rich-unfiled-791c.ii92), and a run of brackets
  parses in linear time.
- Inline rendering walks the inline tree with a stack and appends each run
  of text in one combined style, as Rich's style stack does, so 10,000
  levels of emphasis render in linear time. Adjacent text joins as
  markdown-it's fragments_join joins it.

Markdown draws list markers as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.s3d1) (#431)

* Markdown draws list markers as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.s3d1)

A bullet is " • " in markdown.item.bullet (bold), a number is drawn with no
dot in markdown.item.number (cyan), right-aligned in a column sized for the
number one past the last item, as Rich's last_number sizes it; each hang is
in its marker's style and the item's body in markdown.item. An empty item is
counted and draws nothing. The parser records the list's start number and
leaves the drawing to the renderer.

* A null style is no style to applyStyle; list theme names pinned through Console and documented (rich-unfiled-791c.s3d1)
